question: Roughly what percentage of all waste generated in a healthcare facility is non-hazardous general waste?
explanation: You'd be surprised! The vast majority of hospital waste (around 75% to 90%) is actually regular, non-hazardous stuff from everyday operations, just like household trash. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h1)

question: Why is proper waste sorting so important for you as a nurse?

options.A: It means you never have to wear gloves on the ward
options.B: It cuts down the cost of buying office stationery
options.C: It ensures all hospital trash can be recycled into home items
options.D: It protects staff, patients, and the community from dangerous materials

explanation: Sorting waste correctly keeps everyone safe! It stops nasty accidental injuries and infections from harming healthcare workers, patients, and the public. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h1)

question: Which of these items belongs in the regular, non-hazardous waste bin?

options.A: An IV line dripping with blood
options.B: A surgical blade used in the theatre
options.C: Used food packaging from the admin office
options.D: An expired vial of chemotherapy medication

explanation: Spot on! Office and food packaging has no clinical germs or hazardous chemicals, so it's just regular general waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h2)

question: What is the standard way to handle general, non-hazardous healthcare waste?

options.A: Throw it out through standard municipal waste channels
options.B: Burn it in a high-temperature medical furnace
options.C: Soak it immediately in concentrated chlorine
options.D: Seal it inside heavy-gauge puncture-proof plastic containers

explanation: Because general waste doesn't carry special health risks, it goes straight to ordinary city landfills or municipal collection systems just like home trash. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h2)

question: Which of these counts as pathological waste?

options.A: Cardboard boxes that held sterile gauze
options.B: Used paper from the nurses' station
options.C: Empty glass bottles from IV fluids
options.D: Human tissue and organs removed during surgery

explanation: Pathological waste specifically means body parts, organs, tissues, or blood components taken out during operations. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h3)

question: A patient's wound dressing is soaked in pus and drainage. Which waste category does it go into?
explanation: Any material heavily soiled with blood, pus, or body fluids can spread infection, so it must go straight into the infectious waste bin. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h3)

question: When should you close, seal, and replace a sharps container?

options.A: Only when it is completely overflowing to save space
options.B: Whenever the outside gets a bit dusty
options.C: When it is about three-quarters full
options.D: At the very end of every month, no matter what

explanation: Safety first! Stopping at three-quarters full prevents people from trying to force more items in and accidentally getting a needle-stick injury. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h4)

question: You just finished giving an IM injection on the ward. What is the safest thing to do right away?

options.A: Leave the used syringe on the medication trolley until later
options.B: Use both hands to carefully slide the plastic cap back on
options.C: Snap the needle off the plastic barrel by hand before throwing it away
options.D: Drop the unsheathed needle and syringe straight into a puncture-proof sharps box

explanation: Never recap or bend needles! Dropping the un-capped syringe straight into the sharps box protects your fingers from accidental pricks. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h4)

question: What makes cytotoxic waste so dangerous to handle?

options.A: It shatters easily into sharp glass pieces
options.B: It glows brightly in the dark without any batteries
options.C: It can cause mutations, birth defects, or cancer
options.D: It attracts flies and mosquitoes to the ward

explanation: Cytotoxic drugs are made to destroy cells, which means they carry serious risks like causing cancer or birth defects if handled carelessly. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h5)

question: What is the proper way to dispose of expired cytotoxic drugs?

options.A: Send them for specialized high-temperature incineration
options.B: Treat them in a low-heat autoclave
options.C: Pour them down the clinical sink with plenty of water
options.D: Bury them in a normal municipal landfill

explanation: Cytotoxic drugs have tough chemical structures, so they need intense, high-temperature incineration to be safely destroyed. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h5)

question: Which of these is a typical source of chemical waste in a hospital?

options.A: Leftover food trays from patient bedsides
options.B: Paper wrappers from sterile surgical gloves
options.C: Discarded lab reagents and cleaning solvents
options.D: Cotton wool balls soaked in sterile water

explanation: You'll find chemical waste coming from cleaning supplies, disinfectants, and laboratory testing chemicals. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h6)

question: How is low-level radioactive waste managed right after it is generated?

options.A: Mixed right inside the ordinary household rubbish bags
options.B: Stored in shielded containers until its radioactivity naturally fades
options.C: Flushed down the sluice room toilet with running water
options.D: Burned openly in the hospital yard to save space

explanation: Radioactivity gets weaker over time on its own. Storing the waste in special shielded containers lets it cool down to safe levels before disposal. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h6)

question: According to standard color-coding rules, which bin color is used for infectious waste?
explanation: Bright yellow bins marked with the biohazard sign are universally used to warn everyone and collect infectious or pathological waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h7)

question: You clear away some empty food cartons and clean paper towels from the nurses' station. Which bin should they go into?
explanation: Since paper towels and food wrappers are non-hazardous general waste, they belong in the ordinary black or brown bin. [learn more](GST114_U6_T10#GST114_U6_T10_h7)
